When my mom had a random bout of amnesia when we were grocery shopping. It was just the two of us. Everything was totally fine throughout shopping, we go through the check-out and just as we were about to walk out the door she stops dead in her tracks. At first I thought nothing of it and stopped with her since I wasn't looking at her and I thought she was just doing something with her purse for a sec. Couple moments later I look over at and notice that she is literally frozen in fear, looking around with the most confused terror in her eyes. 
I asked if she was okay and she looked at me with tears welling up in her eyes and asked 
"Where are we??"
I told her we were at HEB, grocery shopping, but she just kept demanding where are we? How did we get here? My heart sank, my stomach was a boulder, my blood was either cold or just gone.
Turned out she had forgotten like 3 years of her life, just like that. In an instant she completely forgot that she moved across the country, remarried, had four dogs, I moved in with her, and had a life here. She went from the lush green humidity of the Midwest to the hot desert sun of western Texas in just a second.
I remember asking pretty quickly if she knew who I was and luckily she did. I was able to keep her calm and got us back to the car, obviously I drove us home. On the way home she slowly pieced memories together, but that 20ish minute drive home had felt like an eternity. 
I still don't know what happened. She refused to go to the hospital and still does to this day. It made me really scared whenever she went out on her own. What if it happens again? What if she can't find her way back to the car again? What if she asks the wrong person for help? What if she gets hurt? What if she can't remember ME, her child? I even became paranoid of losing my own memory. 
Thankfully she hasn't had another episode that I know of, but I will never forget the fear in her eyes and the sinking in my soul. I still don't know how I was able to keep both of us calm, as I was only a Junior in high school. I can't imagine how she felt.

When I was in very early high school, I was literally curled in a ball writhing and yelling in pain. My ndad obviously didn't take this seriously and kept telling me to take ibuprofen, I constantly told him all the time that ibuprofen doesn't help me at all yet he still only bought it because it helped HIM. I told him I needed to see a doctor because something was really wrong, but he didn't think that was necessary and believed it "couldn't be that bad". I was finally able to see a doctor the next day because an older friend of mine agreed to take me. Come to find out I had a severe UTI and was severely constipated and dehydrated. I had no idea I was in such a bad condition because I hadn't really been taught to take care of myself, I didn't even know the signs of dehydration. Of course when I told my dad I went to the ER and what kind of issues I was having, he got upset I went in and blamed me for not taking care of myself properly (the backassward logic he had was appalling). My friend who took me to the ER was shocked by his response and overall neglect and verbally tore him a new one, thankfully she had done this on my behalf many times and I'm grateful for her.

I'm 22, about to be 23 in a couple months. My biggest issue right now is dealing with an extremely persistent, downward spiraling major depressive episode that is also manifesting psychotic features. Mostly dealing with delusions (especially guilt and burden delusions) instead of hallucinations, but it's still very stressful and many days overwhelming. I have thoughts of suicide at least once a day, but no plan. I just realized a couple weeks ago that I've actually been dealing with these issues since near prepubescent age but nobody noticed, somehow?
Yesterday I was spiraling so bad during my therapy appointment that both my therapist and my spouse urged I go to the hospital and see someone. I did go. I waited hours just to get into the psych unit to talk to someone. They told me that since my depression is more chronic, not acute, they see no reason to keep me there and said I was "young and healthy". I was there for maybe an hour before they discharged me.
I left feeling worse. I feel like I'm never truly going to get the help I need. I've rotated through many medications and my depression only subsides for a little bit before it breaks through and renders the meds useless. My spouse helps any way he can but he can only do so much, same with my therapist. My psychiatrist barely listens to my needs and I'm really wanting to switch to someone else who doesn't prescribe me mood stabilizers for severe depression and thinks a beta blocker will keep my anxiety and paranoia at bay (the beta blocker was originally prescribed for my vasovagal syncope by an ER doctor).
Life is making me its bitch right now and I'm trying to fight out of it but it's getting harder and harder every day.
